processing: Made as other Yunnan raw pu-erh usually is: wilted, pan-fired, rolled and sun-dried into mao cha, then sold loose or pressed without any ripening pile.
harvest_season: As across Mengku, spring is the prized picking; autumn lots also exist and are usually cheaper.
appearance_dry: Thick, dark green strips with round stems, sturdy leaves and some visible down.
appearance_wet: Large, fleshy Mengku leaves that open fully, yellow-green with thick stems.
taste_profile: Described as high-toned and honeyed, with a smooth full body, a slightly firmer bitter and astringent edge than Bingdao, and strong mouth-watering at the cheeks and under the tongue.

brewing.notes: Use a gaiwan and keep the early steeps short; the bitterness builds quickly in young large-leaf tea.

vintage_note: Sold by harvest year like other village-named raw pu-erh, as pressed cakes or loose mao cha, mostly young spring tea. Prices separate larger-tree from old-tree material, so ask which you are buying. The village name carries a premium, so it pays to buy from someone who can say where the leaf came from.
description:
Xiaohusai is a small Mengku tea village in Shuangjiang County, about 18 km north of Mengku town, on the slope of the Daxueshan massif. Drinkers know it for the nickname 'sai Bingdao', roughly 'rivals Bingdao', because its aroma and sweetness get compared with its far pricier neighbour.

The leaf is Mengku large-leaf, and it is handled the way raw pu-erh usually is: pan-fired, rolled and sun-dried, then pressed or left loose. Nothing about the method is unique to the village, so the character comes from the trees and the place.

The usual description runs honey and a high aroma, a smooth, thick body and strong salivation, with a little more bitterness and grip than Bingdao has. Most of those notes come from tea sellers, so treat them as a starting point. Brew it hot with short steeps and let the bitterness show you how far to push it.

The tea is sold by year, and the price gap between larger trees and old trees is wide. A price list for Yunnan spring teas put old-tree Xiaohusai well below Bingdao, which is exactly why the comparison is popular. If you like Bingdao's sweetness but not its price, this is a sensible tea to try next to it.
history:
Xiaohusai belongs to the Gongnong village committee of Mengku town. It has one Han and two Lahu settlements, and Lahu people make up about 70% of its population. Some tea gardens near Chashanhe date from 1958 and others from the Republican period.

The old garden at Liangzi covers more than 300 acres by one local account. Some of its largest trees are thought to go back to the Ming dynasty or earlier, which is an estimate from tree size and not a documented date. Little else is recorded about the tea before the recent interest in single-village pu-erh.
